sentences.text: Post-discharge transition call, two business days after an inpatient discharge from Riverbend General Hospital (fictional) on Fri 6 Nov at 16:45. The ADT message carried no diagnosis.

The discharge medication list received Fri 6 Nov 19:30 lists furosemide 80 mg daily, marked changed, and sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily, marked new. The discharge summary was requested on 6 Nov at 18:00 and has not been received.
Member reports breathlessness climbing the stairs since Saturday, with none at rest, no chest pain and ankle swelling that settles overnight.
Weight is up about 2 lb since Friday, weighed at the pharmacy on Saturday. There is no scale at home, so daily weights are not being taken.
Member read the label on the bottle in his hand: furosemide 40 mg. He has not started the 80 mg dose on the discharge list.
Sacubitril/valsartan was never collected. The pharmacy quoted a $47 copay and the member left it at the counter.
The dose discrepancy appears to be because the discharge instructions were not reviewed with the member at the bedside.
sentences.basis: Pattern across recent discharges where the member-reported dose matched the pre-admission fill. The member did not say this.

sentences.text: Cost appears to be the main barrier across the member's whole medication list.
sentences.basis: One quoted copay generalised to the other four drugs. Nothing on this call supports it.

sentences.text: Home-health authorization has been pending since Fri 6 Nov. Plan readmission risk is 0.31, scored 31 Oct, which is before this admission.

Next contact agreed for Thu 12 Nov at 09:30. Member repeated back the three actions: the pharmacy will be called about the copay, a scale is being ordered, and Dr. Rook (fictional) will be asked which furosemide dose to take.
